Zilu asked to go and summon him. Confucius said: "Desist. He knows that I am preoccupied with him. He knows that I am traveling to Chu, and he assumes that I will surely have the King of Chu summon him. He will regard me as a flatterer <note>original: 佞人 <term>nìngrén</term> <gloss>flatterer; sycophant</gloss></note>. If that is the case, he would be ashamed even to hear the words of a flatterer, let alone see the man himself. How could he remain there?" Zilu went to check, and the room was indeed empty. The border guard of Changwu asked Zimu: "When you govern, do not be rash. When you rule the people, do not be destructive. In the past..."

<summary>Confucius explains to Zilu why a certain recluse refuses to meet him, followed by a dialogue between a border guard and Zimu regarding the principles of governance.</summary>
<keywords>Confucius, Zilu, governance, reclusion, moral integrity, Zimu, Changwu</keywords>
